newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rostelekom active amid mixed Russian shares.
newsitem.headline: Rostelekom active amid mixed Russian shares.

text.p: Long-distance operator Rostelekom was volatile on news shareholders abolished a five percent cap on shareholdings but doubled approved capital but other Russian shares were quietly mixed on Thursday, dealers said.
Most leading shares closed around previous levels as Russian players, like Western investors, started vacations.
The Russian Trading System 21-share index firmed to 555.23 after fluctuating during the day and closing on Wednesday at 552.62.
"The market was very quiet," said Trinfiko trader Ilya Galtsov. "There is no clear trend -- it goes up a little bit then it goes down a little bit."

Traders said the market reacted positively to news late in the session that Rostelekom RTKM.RTS had scrapped the five percent limit on individual shareholdings, although a later announcement that shareholders had voted to double capital canceled it out.

"First there was the information that the limit was taken off and it went up and then the news about capital cooled the speculators off," said Rinaco Plus trader Valery Levit, adding that the market had discounted the capital increase long ago.
Rostelekom ticked up to $4.89 on the news after closing on Wednesday at $4.76 but recovered to close at $4.82.
"Overall it is neutral," Levit said, although he added he saw further speculation in the shares on Friday.
National power company UES firmed to $0.4425 after $0.4385 while regional utility Mosenergo ticked up to $1.71 from $1.710.
Galtsov said a slipping Dow Jones index was not affecting Russian shares but another Western trader said the market was feeling the effects of a general world equities malaise.

"It is something Western clients pay attention to and Russian brokers are paying more and more attention to it," the trader said, adding the market was still healthy with neither buyers or sellers dominating trade.
"U.S. instability is giving Russia a reason to take a break."
